clues: A crescent-shaped anatomical landmark located roughly halfway between the umbilicus and pubic symphysis.
The inferior epigastric vessels pass anterior to this border to enter the posterior aspect of the rectus abdominis.
It marks the lower limit of the posterior layer of the rectus sheath.
An anatomical region in the lower anterior abdominal wall bounded inferiorly by the inguinal ligament.
Its lateral border is formed by the inferior epigastric vessels and its medial border by the rectus abdominis.
Direct inguinal hernias protrude directly through this triangle.
A natural anatomical opening situated posterior to the free edge of the lesser omentum.
It is bounded posteriorly by the inferior vena cava and superiorly by the caudate lobe of the liver.
It serves as the sole communication between the greater sac and the omental bursa.
A peritoneal space situated in the supracolic compartment on the right side of the abdomen.
It lies between the visceral surface of the right lobe of the liver and the right kidney.
It is the lowest dependent part of the upper peritoneal cavity in a supine patient.
A fibromuscular band arising from the right crus of the diaphragm.
It suspends and elevates the sharp bend where the fourth part of the duodenum meets the jejunum.
Clinicians use this landmark to divide upper from lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
Three longitudinal ribbons visible on the external surface of the large intestine.
They are formed by concentrated bands of outer longitudinal smooth muscle that converge at the base of the appendix.
Because they are shorter than the bowel wall, they pucker the colon into sacculations called haustra.
A congenital outpouching found on the antimesenteric border of the distal small intestine.
It follows the rule of twos and may contain ectopic gastric or pancreatic mucosa.
It represents a persistent remnant of the embryonic omphalomesenteric or vitelline duct.

terms.sub: Liver, Biliary Tract, Pancreas, and Spleen
clues: An important surgical space bounded superiorly by the inferior surface of the liver.
Its medial boundary is the common hepatic duct and its inferior boundary is the cystic duct.
Surgeons dissect this cystohepatic space to identify and ligate the cystic artery during cholecystectomy.

terms.sub: Liver, Biliary Tract, Pancreas, and Spleen
clues: An imaginary surgical plane running along the course of the middle hepatic vein.
It extends from the gallbladder fossa anteriorly to the inferior vena cava posteriorly.
It divides the liver into functional right and left hemilivers.

terms.sub: Liver, Biliary Tract, Pancreas, and Spleen
clues: A hook-like projection arising from the inferior left part of the head of the pancreas.
It passes medially behind the superior mesenteric artery and vein.
It rests directly anterior to the abdominal aorta.
A clinical sign seen on the anterior abdominal wall in patients with severe portal hypertension.
It results from engorged paraumbilical veins anastomosing with superficial and inferior epigastric veins.
Dilated subcutaneous veins radiate outward from the umbilicus resembling serpents.
A dense connective tissue sheath enclosing the kidney and suprarenal gland along with their surrounding fat.
It separates the perirenal fat inside from the pararenal fat outside.
It is also known as the renal fascia.
A dilated retroperitoneal lymphatic sac situated anterior to the first and second lumbar vertebrae.
It lies immediately to the right of the abdominal aorta and receives the intestinal and lumbar lymphatic trunks.
It tapers superiorly to become the thoracic duct.
A mixed peripheral nerve formed by the anterior divisions of L2, L3, and L4.
It is the sole branch of the lumbar plexus to emerge from the medial border of the psoas major muscle.
It traverses the lateral pelvic wall and exits through a canal to supply the medial thigh adductors.
The shortest anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic inlet.
It extends from the sacral promontory to the nearest point on the posterior surface of the pubic symphysis.
It cannot be measured directly on vaginal exam and is estimated by subtracting 1.5 to 2 cm from the diagonal conjugate.
A flat, pyramid-shaped muscle originating from the anterior surface of the sacrum.
It passes out of the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen to insert on the greater trochanter.
It divides the greater sciatic foramen into suprapiriform and infrapiriform compartments.
The thickest, medial-most muscular component of the levator ani.
It arises from the body of the pubis and loops posteriorly around the anorectal junction without attaching to the coccyx.
It forms a U-shaped sling that maintains the anorectal angle and fecal continence.
A smooth, triangular region located on the internal posterior wall of the urinary bladder.
Its mucosa remains smooth even when the bladder is empty because it is firmly adherent to the underlying muscle.
Its three corners are formed by the two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice.
Visceral motor fibers arising from the anterior rami of S2, S3, and S4.
They stimulate contraction of the detrusor muscle and relaxation of the internal urethral sphincter.
They carry preganglionic parasympathetic innervation to the hindgut and pelvic viscera.
A prominent median elevation on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra.
It bears the blind-ending opening of the prostatic utricle in its center.
The right and left ejaculatory ducts open onto its surface on either side of the utricle.
A dense fibromuscular septum formed by embryonic fusion of the rectovesical peritoneal pouch.
It forms a surgical plane separating the anterior wall of the rectum from the lower urinary tract.
It lies immediately posterior to the prostate gland and seminal vesicles.
A dense condensation of endopelvic fascia extending from the cervix to the lateral pelvic wall.
It encloses the uterine vessels and provides the main passive support against uterine prolapse.
It is also known as the transverse cervical ligament or ligament of Mackenrodt.
The most dependent peritoneal recess in the female pelvic cavity when upright.
It lies between the posterior wall of the uterus and upper vagina anteriorly and the rectum posteriorly.
It is separated from the posterior vaginal fornix only by the vaginal wall and peritoneum.
A somatic motor and sensory nerve arising from S2, S3, and S4.
It exits the greater sciatic foramen, hooks around the ischial spine, and enters the lesser sciatic foramen.
It is the primary nerve of the perineum and external anal and urethral sphincters.
A vascular variant located on the posterior surface of the superior pubic ramus.
It represents an arterial or venous anastomosis between the obturator and inferior epigastric systems.
Its name means crown of death due to severe hemorrhage if injured during femoral hernia or pelvic surgery.
A horizontal fascial tunnel located along the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa.
It is formed by a splitting of the fascia covering the obturator internus muscle.
It conducts the internal pudendal vessels and pudendal nerve toward the urogenital triangle.
An irregular circumferential landmark in the anal canal formed by the inferior margins of the anal valves.
It marks the embryological junction between the endodermal hindgut and ectodermal proctodeum.
It separates visceral painless mucosa above from somatic painful anoderm below.
A fibromuscular node situated in the midline between the anal canal and the urogenital structures.
It lies at the center of the transverse line connecting the two ischial tuberosities.
It anchors the bulbospongiosus, transverse perineal muscles, external anal sphincter, and levator ani.
A tough, dense fibrous sleeve surrounding the corpora cavernosa and corpus spongiosum.
It is continuous proximally with the suspensory ligament and superficial perineal muscles.
It covers the deep dorsal vein, dorsal arteries, and dorsal nerves of the penis.
